title: Store transcript segments and AI summaries as sidecar files per recording
context: Recordings were stored as one metadata JSON plus a plain transcript text file. The commit adds timed Whisper segments, transcript editing, AI notes, and a backup on re-transcribe. The input does not state an explicit motivation beyond these features.
decision: Each recording's extra data is kept as sibling files named by recording id: <id>.segments.json for timed segments, <id>.prev.txt for the previous transcript, and <id>.summary.json and <id>.summary.md for AI notes (the summary JSON is stored as-is). Metadata carries only the transcript flags and summary field. Writes go through a new writeAtomic helper (temp file, then rename). Deletion moves all sidecars into _deleted/ with metadata last, and list() skips sidecar files by checking the id stem against ID_RE. Listing exposes the segments/edited flags and the summary from metadata without reading the sidecar files.
consequences: Listing stays a single metadata read per recording; sidecar files are read only when needed.
Deleting a recording moves every sidecar into _deleted/, and trashFiles never overwrites earlier trash entries.
Sidecar naming (<id>.segments.json, <id>.summary.json) relies on ID_RE to keep them out of the metadata listing.
Transcript text and segments can diverge, since they are separate files; the diff does not show how edits keep them in sync.
Segment and text sizes are capped (MAX_SEGMENTS = 50000, MAX_TEXT_BYTES = 5 MB).
Failures return JSON errors, and readJson maps a missing file to a 404.
The rest of the update() logic, including how .prev.txt is written, is cut off in the input, so its behavior is unverified here.
